# Run bootstrap on Pearson correlation
```{r}
library(mgcv)
library(dplyr)
library(boot)
library(boot.pval)
library(parallel)

set.seed(1)

boot_n <- 5000
nets <- 1:17
network_vars <- sprintf("PFN%02d", nets)

dout <- "../../Results/Scatterplots/22q_boot"
dir.create(dout, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare common complete-case sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nets <- 1:17
network_vars <- sprintf("PFN%02d", nets)

required_vars <- c(
  network_vars,
  "stat_22q",
  "TC_area",
  "sex",
  "euler",
  "median_fd_combined",
  "age",
  "subclass"
)

analysis_dat <- matched_all %>%
  filter(
    if_all(all_of(required_vars), ~ !is.na(.))
  )

analysis_dat <- droplevels(analysis_dat)

stopifnot(
  nlevels(analysis_dat$stat_22q) == 2,
  identical(levels(analysis_dat$stat_22q), c("0", "1")),
  all(is.finite(analysis_dat$TC_area)),
  all(analysis_dat$TC_area > 0),
  all(as.matrix(analysis_dat[, network_vars]) > 0),
  !anyDuplicated(analysis_dat$subject)
)

cat("Analysis sample:", nrow(analysis_dat), "\n")
print(table(analysis_dat$stat_22q))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Import normative allometry coefficients
# ------------------------------------------------------------

PNC_PFN_func_effects <- read.csv(
  "../../Results/PNC_PFN_Func_Temp/log_log_temp_func_area_summary_results.csv"
)

pnc_allometry_beta <- PNC_PFN_func_effects$beta

stopifnot(
  length(pnc_allometry_beta) == 17,
  all(is.finite(pnc_allometry_beta))
)

# Verify the CSV rows are ordered PFN01-PFN17.


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate observed Figure 6B statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

observed_beta_22q <- numeric(17)

for (net in nets) {

  model_dat <- analysis_dat
  model_dat$y <- log(model_dat[[network_vars[net]]])

  fit <- gam(
    y ~ stat_22q +
      log(TC_area) +
      sex +
      euler +
      median_fd_combined +
      s(age, k = 4) +
      s(subclass, bs = "re"),
    data = model_dat,
    method = "REML"
  )

  observed_beta_22q[net] <- unname(
    coef(fit)[["stat_22q1"]]
  )
}

names(observed_beta_22q) <- network_vars

observed_r <- cor(
  pnc_allometry_beta,
  observed_beta_22q,
  method = "pearson"
)

observed_slope <- unname(
  coef(lm(observed_beta_22q ~ pnc_allometry_beta))[2]
)

observed_stats <- c(
  observed_beta_22q,
  pearson_r = observed_r,
  slope = observed_slope
)

cat("Observed Pearson r:", observed_r, "\n")
cat("Observed slope:", observed_slope, "\n")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create dataframe of unique matched subclasses
# ------------------------------------------------------------

subclass_df <- data.frame(
  subclass = unique(as.character(analysis_dat$subclass))
)

n_subclasses <- nrow(subclass_df)

cat("Number of subclasses:", n_subclasses, "\n")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Bootstrap statistic
#
# Resample complete matched subclasses with replacement.
# The SAME bootstrap sample is used for all 17 networks.
#
# Returns:
# 1-17: genotype coefficients
# 18: Pearson correlation
# 19: cross-network regression slope
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_figure6B_stat <- function(
    full_data,
    normative_beta,
    network_names
) {

  # Capture inputs in the function environment.
  # This allows the statistic to run on Windows PSOCK workers.
  full_data <- full_data
  normative_beta <- as.numeric(normative_beta)
  network_names <- as.character(network_names)

  genotype_levels <- levels(full_data$stat_22q)
  sex_levels <- levels(full_data$sex)

  function(cluster_data, indices) {

    sampled_subclasses <- as.character(
      cluster_data$subclass[indices]
    )

    # Reconstruct participant-level bootstrap sample
    d_list <- lapply(
      seq_along(sampled_subclasses),
      function(i) {

        original_subclass <- sampled_subclasses[i]

        tmp <- full_data[
          as.character(full_data$subclass) == original_subclass,
          ,
          drop = FALSE
        ]

        # Assign a unique random-effect ID for each
        # occurrence of a sampled subclass
        tmp$boot_subclass <- paste0("boot_", i)

        tmp
      }
    )

    d <- dplyr::bind_rows(d_list)

    # Preserve factor reference levels
    d$stat_22q <- factor(
      d$stat_22q,
      levels = genotype_levels
    )

    d$sex <- factor(
      d$sex,
      levels = sex_levels
    )

    d$boot_subclass <- factor(
      d$boot_subclass
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Fit 17 GAMs to the SAME resampled subjects
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    beta_22q <- numeric(length(network_names))

    for (net in seq_along(network_names)) {

      PFN_area <- network_names[net]

      d$y <- log(d[[PFN_area]])

      fit <- mgcv::gam(
        y ~
          stat_22q +
          log(TC_area) +
          sex +
          euler +
          median_fd_combined +
          s(age, k = 4) +
          s(boot_subclass, bs = "re"),
        data = d,
        method = "REML"
      )

      beta_22q[net] <- unname(
        coef(fit)[["stat_22q1"]]
      )
    }

    if (!all(is.finite(beta_22q))) {
      stop("Non-finite genotype coefficient.")
    }

    if (sd(beta_22q) == 0) {
      stop("Zero variance in network genotype coefficients.")
    }

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Figure 6B Pearson correlation
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    r <- cor(
      normative_beta,
      beta_22q,
      method = "pearson"
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Figure 6B regression slope
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    slope <- unname(
      coef(lm(beta_22q ~ normative_beta))[2]
    )

    c(
      setNames(beta_22q, network_names),
      pearson_r = r,
      slope = slope
    )
  }
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Construct statistic
# ------------------------------------------------------------

figure6B_stat <- make_figure6B_stat(
  full_data = analysis_dat,
  normative_beta = pnc_allometry_beta,
  network_names = network_vars
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Parallel processing
#
# Limit to 8 workers to avoid excessive RAM use.
# Increase if sufficient memory is available.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

n_cores <- max(
  1,
  min(8, parallel::detectCores() - 2)
)

cat("Using", n_cores, "workers\n")

cl <- parallel::makeCluster(n_cores)

# Load required packages on workers
invisible(parallel::clusterEvalQ(cl, {
  library(mgcv)
  library(boot)
  library(dplyr)
}))

# Reproducible independent RNG streams
parallel::clusterSetRNGStream(
  cl,
  iseed = 1
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Run bootstrap
# ------------------------------------------------------------

boot_figure6B <- tryCatch(
  {
    boot::boot(
      data = subclass_df,
      statistic = figure6B_stat,
      R = boot_n,
      parallel = "snow",
      ncpus = n_cores,
      cl = cl
    )
  },
  finally = {
    parallel::stopCluster(cl)
  }
)

colnames(boot_figure6B$t) <- names(observed_stats)

saveRDS(
  boot_figure6B,
  paste0(dout, "/Figure6B_boot_object.rds")
)

cat("Bootstrap completed.\n")
```

## Get 95% CIs
```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract bootstrap statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

boot_r <- boot_figure6B$t[, "pearson_r"]
boot_slope <- boot_figure6B$t[, "slope"]

stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(boot_figure6B$t)),
  all(is.finite(boot_r)),
  all(is.finite(boot_slope)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    as.numeric(boot_figure6B$t0),
    as.numeric(observed_stats),
    tolerance = 1e-6
  ))
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate empirical influence values ONCE per statistic
#
# type = "jack" uses leave-one-subclass-out jackknife.
#
# Because boot_figure6B$data contains one row per subclass,
# jackknife deletions operate at the matched-subclass level.
#
# Index 18 = Pearson r
# Index 19 = regression slope
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("Calculating jackknife influence values for Pearson r...\n")

L_r <- boot::empinf(
  boot.out = boot_figure6B,
  index = 18,
  type = "jack"
)

cat("Calculating jackknife influence values for slope...\n")

L_slope <- boot::empinf(
  boot.out = boot_figure6B,
  index = 19,
  type = "jack"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Verify influence values
# ------------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(
  length(L_r) == n_subclasses,
  length(L_slope) == n_subclasses,
  all(is.finite(L_r)),
  all(is.finite(L_slope))
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Save influence values to avoid recalculation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  list(
    L_r = L_r,
    L_slope = L_slope
  ),
  paste0(dout, "/Figure6B_jackknife_influence.rds")
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# BCa 95% confidence intervals
#
# Supply precomputed L values.
# This prevents boot.ci() from calculating them again.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

r_CI <- boot::boot.ci(
  boot_figure6B,
  type = c("bca", "perc"),
  index = 18,
  L = L_r
)

slope_CI <- boot::boot.ci(
  boot_figure6B,
  type = c("bca", "perc"),
  index = 19,
  L = L_slope
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract BCa and percentile intervals
# ------------------------------------------------------------

r_CI_95 <- r_CI$bca[4:5]
slope_CI_95 <- slope_CI$bca[4:5]

r_perc_95 <- r_CI$percent[4:5]
slope_perc_95 <- slope_CI$percent[4:5]


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Two-sided BCa p-values from CI inversion
#
# Pass the SAME influence values to boot.pval().
#
# H0: r = 0
# H1: r != 0
#
# H0: slope = 0
# H1: slope != 0
# ------------------------------------------------------------

r_p <- boot.pval::boot.pval(
  boot_figure6B,
  type = "bca",
  theta_null = 0,
  alternative = "two.sided",
  index = 18,
  L = L_r
)

slope_p <- boot.pval::boot.pval(
  boot_figure6B,
  type = "bca",
  theta_null = 0,
  alternative = "two.sided",
  index = 19,
  L = L_slope
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Print results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat(
  "\nObserved Pearson r:", observed_r,
  "\nPearson BCa 95% CI:", r_CI_95,
  "\nPearson percentile 95% CI:", r_perc_95,
  "\nPearson BCa two-sided p:", r_p,
  "\n\nObserved slope:", observed_slope,
  "\nSlope BCa 95% CI:", slope_CI_95,
  "\nSlope percentile 95% CI:", slope_perc_95,
  "\nSlope BCa two-sided p:", slope_p,
  "\n"
)

print(r_CI)
print(slope_CI)
```

write.csv(
  observed_network_out,
  paste0(dout, "/Figure6B_observed_network_coefficients.csv"),

)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Save observed correlation, slope, CIs, p-values, percentile intervals
# ------------------------------------------------------------
boot_summary_out <- data.frame(
  statistic = c("pearson_r", "slope"),

  observed = c(
    observed_r,
    observed_slope
  ),

  BCa_CI_lower = c(
    r_CI_95[1],
    slope_CI_95[1]
  ),

  BCa_CI_upper = c(
    r_CI_95[2],
    slope_CI_95[2]
  ),

  percentile_CI_lower = c(
    r_perc_95[1],
    slope_perc_95[1]
  ),

  percentile_CI_upper = c(
    r_perc_95[2],
    slope_perc_95[2]
  ),

  p_bca_two_sided = c(
    r_p,
    slope_p
  ),

  n_boot = boot_n,
  n_subclasses = n_subclasses
)

write.csv(
  boot_summary_out,
  paste0(dout, "/Figure6B_boot_BCa_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Examine bootstrap dist and jackknife influence
```{r}
data.frame(
  statistic = c("Pearson r", "Slope"),

  observed = c(observed_r, observed_slope),

  bootstrap_mean = c(
    mean(boot_r),
    mean(boot_slope)
  ),

  bootstrap_median = c(
    median(boot_r),
    median(boot_slope)
  ),

  bootstrap_sd = c(
    sd(boot_r),
    sd(boot_slope)
  ),

  proportion_positive = c(
    mean(boot_r >= 0),
    mean(boot_slope >= 0)
  )
)

summary(L_r)
summary(L_slope)

# BCa acceleration parameters
bca_acceleration <- function(L) {
  sum(L^3) / (6 * sum(L^2)^(3/2))
}

c(
  acceleration_r = bca_acceleration(L_r),
  acceleration_slope = bca_acceleration(L_slope)
)

# BCa bias-correction term
get_z0 <- function(draws, observed) {
  qnorm(mean(draws < observed))
}

z0_r <- get_z0(boot_r, observed_r)
z0_slope <- get_z0(boot_slope, observed_slope)

# BCa-adjusted percentile positions for a 95% CI
get_bca_probs <- function(z0, a) {

  z <- qnorm(c(0.025, 0.975))

  pnorm(
    z0 + (z0 + z) / (1 - a * (z0 + z))
  )
}

bca_probs_r <- get_bca_probs(
  z0_r,
  0.002398259
)

bca_probs_slope <- get_bca_probs(
  z0_slope,
  0.004704048
)

data.frame(
  statistic = c("Pearson r", "Slope"),
  z0 = c(z0_r, z0_slope),
  lower_quantile = c(bca_probs_r[1], bca_probs_slope[1]),
  upper_quantile = c(bca_probs_r[2], bca_probs_slope[2]),
  lower_order_position = 5000 * c(
    bca_probs_r[1],
    bca_probs_slope[1]
  ),
  proportion_positive = c(
    mean(boot_r >= 0),
    mean(boot_slope >= 0)
  )
)
```
